texts: When a left atrial mass excised from the septum with only its endocardium turns out on frozen section to be a sarcoma, the next step is full-thickness resection of the atrial septum with clear margins, closed with a pericardial patch.
Complete resection with negative margins is the most important factor for survival in cardiac sarcoma.
A shave of the endocardium leaves tumour in the septum, and closing then means a certain recurrence.
Chemotherapy and radiation are added after resection, not instead of it, and transplantation is not a first-line treatment for a resectable sarcoma.
